open_points.subject: Acceptance status of R0-19 and R0-20
open_points.text: “Accepted by the owner as a whole on 2026-10-26” contradicts the inclusion of “R0-19 — ... (owner, 2026-10-27)” and “R0-20 — ... (owner, 2026-10-27)”.
open_points.question: Were R0-19 and R0-20 accepted as amendments to State 0, and what is the effective acceptance date of the whole document?
options: R0-19 and R0-20 are accepted amendments and the effective acceptance date is 2026-10-27
R0-19 and R0-20 are accepted separately while the original whole remains dated 2026-10-26
R0-19 and R0-20 are not yet accepted inputs
open_points.default_guess: Treat R0-19 and R0-20 as accepted amendments and State 0 as effectively accepted on 2026-10-27.

open_points.subject: Decision provenance claim
open_points.text: “every decision below names the v1 decision (V1-n) or the legacy finding (Ln) it keeps, narrows or replaces” is false for decisions including R0-15, R0-16, R0-17, R0-19 and R0-20, which name no V1-n or Ln source.
open_points.question: Must each of these decisions be given a V1/legacy source, or is the universal provenance claim incorrect?
options: Add the missing V1/L provenance to every decision
Limit the provenance claim to decisions that actually cite a V1/L source
Treat the uncited decisions as having no predecessor
open_points.default_guess: Treat the universal provenance sentence as stale and allow uncited decisions to have no predecessor.

open_points.subject: Browser access across the network boundary
open_points.text: “Browser — the Registry frontend from its own origin; CORS admits exactly that origin” and the exclusion saying the frontend is a client of the Registry API conflict with “An instance reachable from beyond its host is a wrong deployment”.
open_points.question: How does a frontend running in a user's browser reach Registry without making Registry reachable beyond its host?
options: The browser and frontend origin exist only on the Registry host
A frontend server or gateway proxies browser requests to Registry, so the browser is not a direct Registry client
Registry is exposed to the browser through an allowed external route, narrowing R0-19
open_points.default_guess: Use a frontend-side server or gateway as the Registry client and remove the browser as a direct trust-boundary actor.

open_points.subject: Secret non-disclosure guarantee
open_points.text: “never in a record, a log line or an answer” does not say whether this prohibits only storing or emitting credential fields, or also requires detecting secret values when they appear inside ordinary caller-supplied data; no refusal or redaction behavior is defined.
open_points.question: What exact inputs and outputs are covered by the secret non-disclosure promise, and what must happen when ordinary submitted data equals or contains a configured secret?
options: Prevent credentials and authentication material from being deliberately persisted or emitted, without scanning ordinary domain data
Reject domain data that equals or contains any configured secret
Accept the data but redact matching secret text from records, logs and answers
open_points.default_guess: Apply the guarantee structurally to authentication material and never log or return credential values, without content-scanning ordinary domain fields.
